# Dakarakkhasajātaka (Ja 517)

**ID:** Ja 517
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Dakarakkhasajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul15.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In the standard edition of the text, it is situated between the *Mahākapijātaka* and the *Paṇḍarajātaka* [Fausböll 1891]. Rather than reciting an independent narrative, the canonical entry provides only an opening verse lemma (*Sace vo vuyhamānānan ti*) and defers the full exposition with the explicit cross-reference noting that the entire account will be set forth in the *Mahāummagga-jātaka* (*Taṃ sabbaṃ Mahāummaggajātake āvibhavissati*) [Fausböll 1891].

In the later *Mahāummagga* narrative cycle, this episode is treated as the *Dakarakkhasa-pañha* ("Question of the Water Ogre") [Fausböll 1896]. There, King Cūḷanī describes whom he would successively surrender to a water ogre (*dakarakkhasa*)—including mother, wife, brother, friend, and himself—to protect the Great Being (Mahosadha Paṇḍita), concluding the question when this test of devotion is publicly proclaimed before the citizens [Fausböll 1896].

 Automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus confirms that the text shares 63 passages internally within the Pali corpus, heavily concentrated in the sixth volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (47 matches), reflecting the inclusion of the narrative in the *Mahāummagga*, as well as 16 matches with the grammatical text *Saddanītippakaraṇaṃ* (*Dhātumālā*) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects low-scoring passage matches in Tibetan Buddhist texts, such as the *Buddhacarita* (D4156), the *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155-2), the *Karmaśataka* (D0340), and the *Jātakamālā* (D4150) [DharmaNexus].
